## Chapter purpose

Develop probability as the language of uncertainty, beginning with intuitive events and progressing to random variables and distributions.

## Topics

::: {.statx-topic-grid}
::: {.statx-topic-card}
<span>3.1–3.2</span>
### Rules and conditions
Probability rules, intuition, dependence, independence, and conditional probability.
:::
::: {.statx-topic-card}
<span>3.3</span>
### Bayes’ theorem
Update prior understanding when new evidence becomes available.
:::
::: {.statx-topic-card}
<span>3.4</span>
### Random variables
Connect uncertain outcomes to numerical quantities.
:::
::: {.statx-topic-card}
<span>3.5</span>
### Distributions
Bernoulli, binomial, Poisson, uniform, and normal distributions.
:::
